question: What will the ONS's first estimate of UK GDP growth be for Q3 2026 (quarter-on-quarter)?

calls.reasoning: Two of three months known: Jul +0.4, Aug +0.1 m/m; 3m-to-Aug +0.7% vs 3m-to-May. Index arithmetic (Apr -0.1, May +0.1, Jun +0.4) gives Q3 q/q ≈0.75% with flat September; each 1% Sept move shifts Q3 ~0.33pp. September indicators soft (retail sales -0.4%, composite PMI ~51.7 consistent with 0.1% q/q, likely payback from Aug production +0.8%), so expect Sept roughly -0.3 to +0.1, leaving Q3 centred ~0.7. Q2 revised up to 0.5% in QNA (raising base slightly). Polymarket (thin, $54k vol, ONS first-estimate resolution) prices 0.6-0.7 at ~48%, 0.8-0.9 at ~31%, consistent. Model/survey-based forecasts (TE 0.4, HMT survey 0.3) ignore known monthly data and are discounted.
calls.dossier:
- ONS monthly GDP Aug 2026 (pub 15 Oct 2026): Aug +0.1% m/m, Jul +0.4% m/m; 3m to Aug +0.7% vs 3m to May; 3m to Jul and to Jun revised up to 0.5%. Services +0.9% 3m; production -0.2% 3m but +0.8% in Aug alone (manufacturing); construction -1.0% 3m, -0.2% in Aug; July construction revised down to -0.5%.
- Earlier monthly prints (ONS): Feb +0.4, Mar +0.3, Apr -0.1, May +0.1, Jun +0.4 (original vintages).
- ONS QNA Q2 2026 (30 Sep 2026): Q2 revised up to +0.5% q/q (from 0.4 first est); Q1 +0.6% unrevised; services +0.6, construction +0.8, production -0.1 in Q2.
- Carry-over arithmetic using these monthly indices: Q3 q/q ≈ +0.75% if Sept flat; each 1% Sept m/m change moves Q3 by ~0.33pp. Sept would need ~-2% m/m to bring Q3 near 0.
- ONS retail sales Sept 2026 (pub 23 Oct): -0.4% m/m vs -0.1% expected (warm weather, supermarkets down); Aug +0.7, Jul -0.4; Q3 retail +0.7% 3m/3m.
- S&P Global UK PMI Sept 2026: manufacturing 51.9 (Aug 51.7); flash services/composite ~51.7 vs 52.0 expected; S&P said consistent with ~0.1% quarterly growth; cited energy prices, borrowing costs, policy uncertainty.
- BoE July 2026 MPR projected underlying Q3 growth ~0%; HM Treasury Sept 2026 survey of forecasters reportedly ~0.3% Q3 (survey-based, partly predates Jul/Aug data). Trading Economics model 0.4%.
- Upside: services momentum strong (professional services, IT +2.8% 3m). Downside: possible Sept payback in production after Aug +0.8% rebound; weak construction; July/Aug revisions (typically ±0.1pp on the quarter).
- Human market: Polymarket 'UK GDP growth in Q3 2026 (QoQ)' exists (bucketed, ~$54k volume, ONS bulletin resolution); see forecaster's own check for prices.
- Status quo: first estimate typically lands near carry-over of published months adjusted for third-month indicators.
- Resolves off ONS 'GDP first quarterly estimate, UK: July to September 2026' main-points q/q figure (one decimal), not the 22 Dec QNA revision.
- Event window: Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) measured; publication 12 Nov 2026 07:00 GMT; as of 2026-11-02 quarter 100% elapsed, Jul/Aug published, Sept unpublished.
- Searched but not found: consensus for Sept m/m GDP, Sept index of production/services previews, bank nowcasts for the first estimate; Kalshi/bookmaker UK GDP market (none found).

That gives a carry-over of about 0.77% q/q if September is flat (rounds to 0.8); September at -0.1 to -0.4 gives 0.7, and -0.5 or worse gives 0.6. calls.reasoning: July +0.4 and August +0.1 m/m are on the books, so a flat September gives ~0.75-0.77% q/q. September indicators were soft (retail -0.4% vs -0.1% expected, flash composite PMI 51.7, likely production payback after August's +0.8), which centres September slightly negative and the quarter around 0.7. Revisions to July/August and Blue Book base changes widen the spread both ways. The thin Polymarket market (~$54k, matching ONS first-estimate resolution) reportedly puts ~48% on 0.6-0.7 and ~31% on 0.8-0.9, consistent with this. Survey and stale-consensus figures of 0.3-0.4 ignore the known monthly data and are discounted.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: July +0.4, August +0.1, Q2 revised to 0.5, September retail -0.4, PMI 51.7, Polymarket ~48% on 0.6-0.7. The remaining dispute is the flat-September carry-over (0.75 in runs 1-2 vs 0.77 in run 3). That comes from data vintages and post-Blue Book April/May levels that cannot be checked without web access, so it stays as uncertainty about whether the result rounds to 0.7 or 0.8. How negative September will be is a judgment call; I lean slightly negative given the retail miss and the probable production payback, so the median is 0.7. Undated survey/aggregator figures of 0.3-0.4 are discounted as stale. No mechanism was found for an outcome outside the range (it would need September below about -2% or above about +1.5% m/m), so no escape mass is priced. Run 1's reference class and a similar dispersion are carried forward.
